transcript: Well, it's incredibly important. And I'm sorry that we haven't been able to do it for all Americans. speaker: SPEAKER_00
transcript: Well, you know, my family's actually from Brownsville. My father was a customs agent after World War II and my mom and aunt grew up there and spent a lot of my childhood going there. I can tell you know, the border is a real place. It's not a backdrop for a photo op or somewhere that you should just go. So you can claim that that we're being invaded or to make irresponsible statements. And that's what I've You know, unfortunately seeing just far too much of this kind of like, almost tourism of going to the border and pretending like you're there seeing all these terrible things happening. Listen, we need to have a serious conversation in this country around how we should have a comprehensive reform of our immigration system, including, yes, elements of board security, which we have increased funding for the Board of Patrol and Biden administration is actually increasing the size of the Board of Patrol for the first time in years, but also to meet the needs of our economy and how to make our immigration system work in a way that I think is humane and consistent with our values. And so I'm glad that President Biden, was able to go there and see and hear from local leaders about what's going on, because it's also true that if Venezuela is in collapse, that Haiti is in collapse, that Nicaragua, Honduras, and El Salvador are all extremely chaotic. And these are global trends that are driving enormous flows of people out of those countries. And it's affecting the entire region. And of course, some of it is going to end up at our border. And so we need to have a way to process that and we need to put resources there. And I think it's right for the administration to be surging some resources there, but they're limited in terms of what they can do under their authorities. but they really needed some action from Congress on some comprehensive investments and reforms that will allow them to process asylum seekers more efficiently to really put in place the person power and the policies needed to do this, I think, consistent with who we are as a country. And so I think that's what I hope the president took away from this. I would like to see us find some bipartisan agreement around how we can address our immigration system. We've had a framework before or twice. In fact, President Bush was in office working with Ted Kennedy. They had a framework that then failed in the Republican controlled house. We also had President Biden or Obama was in office, kind of the gang of eight, a framework that failed. We know what it looks like, what that framework looks like. And we need to pick that back up. And maybe this bipartisan group of senators that came down recently, maybe they'll be able to make some progress on their side. Unfortunately, I don't think we'll see much willingness to do that on the house side with the Republican majority, because in some ways, I think it's too salient of a political issue for them to actually solve it. And that would be kind of taking away one of their main talking points if they addressed it. So I'm glad he came and we need to act in the Congress. We haven't had a major reform passed through Congress on the immigration system since President Reagan was in office. I mean, it's time to do something about this.
